note: The site's measured results, comparisons, limits and decisions are these claims; a page uses one as {claim:Cxx} and shows it with its status and qualifier. What a page says Foundry does is held by the site's tests (app/site/test), not registered here, and text other modules write (the n8n import report, the IT brief, the coding agent's replies, card wording) is linted for overclaiming phrases (app/site/test/copy-lint.test.mjs), not registered. app/site/test/claims.test.mjs checks that each source file exists under research/, that each claim cites lines and a short verbatim quote found in them (source.lines, source.quote; source.also for a second file), that every number in a claim's text and qualifier appears within those lines, and that each status and evidence word is one of the lists below. Status words: Works now, Preview, Not re-tested, Planned, Not decided, Decided, Limit, Research result (a result from our research test beds, not something this product does), Literature (published research or vendor data). Evidence words: development (our own tests, not sealed), design, decided, documentation, literature.

C01.text: Nothing real is made or sent until you say yes. Tests on pretend data and new versions are made without asking you. The limit: a coding agent that can run commands as you on this computer could do what you can do, including say yes.
C01.short: Nothing real happens until you say yes (with one honest limit)
C01.qualifier: Our own tests of this site and its tools. Not covered: any program running as you on this computer.

source.anchor: §5, the Turn on and Going live rows; §6, the same-user limit

C02.text: In our tests, 10 of 10 attempts to get around your yes were refused.
C02.short: Ways around your yes are refused
C02.qualifier: Tested on the earlier prototype's tools and page, before the exact-list approval and the one-time links were added; that set of attempts has not been re-run against them. The ways around your yes found in the security review of 2026-10-21 (a printed link read by an agent, a hook answering the dialog, a list changed after you saw it) have their own tests now. Not covered: an agent using your terminal, or a hook Foundry can't see.

C03.text: A test uses pretend data, or your own list if you drop one, and a pretend inbox. Nothing real is made or sent during a test.
C03.short: Tests make and send nothing real

source.quote: a test on the person's own list

C04.text: In our own tests, a low-cost AI that practised first built a 14-case order process with 14 of 14 right, for $0.39. A top AI that built it in one go got 5 of 14, for $7.63.
C04.qualifier: A research test bed, not something this product does: its cards call no AI. One task family we wrote, on one sized-down world of 14 cases, with a complete, correct specification given to both builders; the top AI was run once and made 11 arm errors. Not a promise about your work.

C05.text: On 60 public development tasks, a low-cost AI with Foundry's procedure passed 18 of 60 for $0.94; a stronger AI alone passed 20 of 60 for $6.03.
C05.short: A low-cost AI with a procedure, at about a sixth of the cost
C05.qualifier: A research harness, not something this product does: its cards call no AI. One run each on public development tasks; the frozen test run has not been done.

C06.text: Of 10 sample n8n files, 2 translated into Foundry steps without errors and 8 were refused with reasons. Calling all 10 in place, in n8n, is designed but not built. 0 were run.
C06.short: n8n import: what translates, and what doesn't run yet
C06.qualifier: A small, skewed sample of open-licence files. Nothing was executed, and translating a workflow does not show it behaves as it did in n8n: running one needs connectors Foundry doesn't have yet.

C07.text: In a simulated company, builds that passed their process check still applied 57 of 57 large refunds without approval. With the rule layer, 0 did, but the process check then passed 973 of 1022 cases instead of all of them. A scripted auditor answered four of its five questions in 45 of 45 runs, and the fifth in 41 of 45.
C07.short: Rules that hold at run time (test bed only)
C07.qualifier: A test bed we built; this rule layer is not in the product.

C08.text: Free while one person decides, at any size, with single sign-on included. Paid only when a second person's yes or a rule owner has to count.
C08.qualifier: Decision D2, taken under the owner's general permission: reversible, and the owner may overturn it. No price is set, and no buyer has been asked about it yet.

source.quote: **Free:** one authority, any complexity, SSO included

also.quote: a pricing hypothesis, no buyer interview done

C09.text: Foundry runs only on this computer. Nothing is published or hosted.

C10.text: Bringing your own AI key is free, and the key goes into your computer's keychain, never into files or logs.
C10.qualifier: A keychain keeps the key from other users of this computer, not from programs running as you. On a Mac, Foundry saves the key without naming which programs may read it, so any program running as you can read it back through the security command without a prompt (from Apple's documentation of that command; not tried on a Mac). On Linux, any program running as you can read it while the keyring is unlocked.

source.quote: keys in the OS keychain and never in the repo or logs

C11.text: People approve almost every single prompt (97% in one vendor's data) but reject whole plans far more often (39% versus 3%).
C11.short: Why Foundry asks once, about the whole plan
C11.qualifier: Vendor-published numbers, not a controlled study of Foundry.

C12.text: The earlier prototype went from request to first live run in 3 person actions.
C12.short: Three actions in the earlier prototype
C12.qualifier: Measured once on the earlier prototype's weekly report, by a test that plays the person. This site's own journeys count their steps separately, and this number has not been re-measured on it.

C13.text: Tested on Linux only; macOS and Windows are untested. Steps that run code need a Linux sandbox, so on macOS and Windows they should be refused; that has not been tried there.

C14.text: Your decisions are kept in their own chained log, not inside a run's chained record; an AI builder's transcripts are in neither; and neither record's latest link is kept outside this computer unless you copy it there yourself.

source.quote: decisions and transcripts are not yet bound into the chain

also.quote: comparing both latest links with copies kept elsewhere
